row: PETA (People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals)

You are watching Animal Rights Television®.

People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA) is the largest animal rights organization in the world, and PETA entities have more than 10 million members and supporters globally.

PETA opposes speciesism, a human-supremacist worldview, and focuses its attention on the four areas in which the largest numbers of animals suffer the most intensely for the longest periods of time: in laboratories, in the food industry, in the clothing trade, and in the entertainment business. We also work on a variety of other issues, including the cruel killing of rodents, birds, and other animals who are often considered “pests” as well as cruelty to domesticated animals.

PETA works through public education, investigative news gathering and reporting, research, animal rescue, legislation, special events, celebrity involvement, and protest campaigns.

Ready to get active for animals? Check out http://www.PETA.org

• Emergency rescue from auctions and slaughter routes
• Medical care, rehabilitation, and trauma recovery
• Safety, patience, and respect
• A chance to heal after the storm has passed

They have survived the storm.
Now they deserve gentleness.

Dr. Antonio Webb is a board certified and fellowship trained Orthopedic Spine Surgeon located in San Antonio, Texas who specializes in degenerative, artificial disc replacement, and minimally invasive spine surgery.

Dr. Webb is a highly decorated combat veteran who spent 8 years in the US Air Force as a medic/LVN including a deployment north of Baghdad, Iraq in 2005. His medical training also afforded him the opportunity to perform surgery in Liberia, West Africa, Bangkok, Thailand, and Port Au Prince Haiti.

Dr. Webb completed a combined Neurosurgery/Orthopedic Spine Surgery fellowship at Texas Back Institute. TBI was the first practice in America to implant an artificial disc replacement. He took the best practices from all his mentors to formulate his own unique approach to spine care believing that conservative treatment is the ultimate goal, using surgery only as a final and last resort.

Cats of San Bernardino was started by Jaina and Ivy Spagis when they moved to San Bernardino in 2016
from Los Angeles. They were shocked that San Bernardino did not offer free spay and neuter
services like LA and realized that the feral situation in their new neighborhood was out of
control. They began trapping and spaying/neutering feral cats at their own expense, but soon
realized the problem was too big to tackle on their own.

They have converted their home into an animal sanctuary, providing space for kittens and their
mommas waiting for adoption, rehabilitation areas for recovering injured cats, play areas for
healthy cats. With the help of foster families in the city of San
Bernardino they have as many as 50 cats in their care at one time.Their dream is to one day
have a large property/facility which will help save thousands of more lives. This new property
would have catios, feral enclosures, a medical room, nursery, rehabilitation area, and adoption
center.

Galgos del Sol was founded by Tina Solera & is a registered charity (G30856736) based in Murcia, Spain. 

Recently we have been accepted as a registered USA 501c charity & a UK non profit!

We rescue and rehabilitate abandoned and injured Galgos for placement in forever homes in the UK, Europe, and US. Bred solely for hunting, thousands of Galgos are abandoned or killed annually at the end of each short hunting season. 

Galgos are not typically considered as pets in Spain and their lives end in less than humane ways either in perreras (kill stations) or abandoned to a life of persecution on the streets. 

GDS is passionately committed to the welfare of galgos and works tirelessly to educate the public about their plight & are currently raising funds to build an education & rescue centre. You can find out more about the Centre on our webpage www.galgosdelsol.org

Whether you’re a veterinary or animal science student, a researcher, or simply an animal enthusiast, this channel offers valuable resources to deepen your understanding of the animal body and its incredible adaptations.

We are an amazing sanctuary for feral cats! We are located in Faribault, Minnesota. 

The cats that live here are cats that had to be live trapped as they were completely un-socialized to humans.  

Regular rescues and shelters cannot take in these cats as it can take years for them to be come adoptable.  We have a full time Veterinarian on site for these lucky formerly homeless cats.

Over time, some of these cats gradually learn to trust and love humans and we can adopt them out!  If they don't ever learn to like humans, that is where the word "sanctuary" is important.  They can live out their lives with us.  No threat for euthanasia for lack of space or for being with us too long.  

Please watch our videos and you will see how this truly is a heaven on earth for these cats who lived a life of struggles before coming to us.  Thank you! 😻😻

row: Hi!  I'm Hina Sheth, I have been treating complex orthopedics, sports and pelvic floor physical problems for over 25 years with amazing results.  Now I want to bring my knowledge to the global community so I can spread my knowledge to you. Our bodies are complex systems of 600 muscles and organs intertwined in a fascial system that all work together. Imbalances in this system such as trigger points, visceral and myofascial restrictions can lead to joint, pelvic, and organ issues. Factors like nutrition, exercise, sleep, and stress play a crucial role.  Unfortunately, our current health care model does not look at our bodies as a whole and often times compartmentalize musculoskeletal injuries and dysfunctions.  At Rebalance, our goal is to holistically treat this complex system to restore harmony in the body.  By addressing these imbalances, we help clients improve their overall health and well-being.  Our vision is to empower individuals to create a healthier lifestyle for themselves.

row: On March 29, 1953, KVTV Channel 9 (the forerunner of KCAU-TV) began broadcasting from an improvised studio at Seventh and Pierce Streets. It was the beginnings of the first television station in Sioux City, Iowa. Later in 1956, Channel 9 moved into a historic building at Seventh and Douglas that previously housed the old Sioux City Auditorium and the Tomba Ballroom. KVTV was then a CBS basic station, that also took delayed programs, via kinescope, from NBC, ABC and the Dumont Network. Videotape wasn't a reality until years later, so everything was live or on film. At this time, an invitation was sent to leaders of all fields throughout the country inviting them to participate in a 21st Century Guesstimate. The National University Hospital (NUH) is the leading university hospital in Singapore, and a major tertiary and referral institution. While NUH opened its doors on 24 June 1985, its legacy goes back to the founding of what is today the NUS Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine in 1905.  It is the principal teaching hospital of the medical school and the NUS Faculty of Dentistry.

An Academic Medical Centre under Singapore’s National University Health System, NUH provides affordable specialist care for patients, training for healthcare professionals, and undertakes translational bench-to-bedside research to improve care.

It is the only public and not-for-profit hospital in Singapore to offer a comprehensive suite of specialist care for adults, women and children, as well as paediatric kidney and liver transplant programme.

row: The Royal College of Pathologists is a charity with over 13,000 members worldwide. The majority of members are doctors and scientists working in hospitals and universities in the UK. The College oversees the training of pathologists and scientists working in 17 different specialties, which include cellular pathology, haematology, clinical biochemistry and medical microbiology. Although some pathologists work in laboratories, many work directly with patients in hospitals and the community. Together, they are involved in the majority of all diagnoses and play an important role in disease prevention, treatment, and monitoring. If you have ever had a blood test, cervical smear or tissue biopsy, a pathologist will have been involved in your care.

Welcome to AMR Physiotherapy!

We’re here to guide you on your journey to a healthier, stronger, and more balanced body.

Our focus spans three key areas:
- Rehab to recover from pain and injuries
- Gym training to reduce future injury risks
- Longevity to keep you moving and feeling great for years to come.

If you’ve been hitting the gym or playing sports but are now dealing with more niggles or injuries, this channel is for you. We’ll help you stay fit, look good, and adopt a health-first, well-rounded training approach.

At AMR Physiotherapy, we believe that strengthening often-overlooked areas—like the neck and lower back—should be just as common as training biceps or chest. By addressing these neglected muscles and movements, we aim to help you stay resilient, reduce pain, and enjoy long-term health.

Join us to explore practical rehab tips, targeted exercises, and training techniques that keep your body balanced, strong, and ready for whatever life throws your way.

My name is Johanna Janatuinen, I´m a physiotherapist, animal physiotherapist and riding instructor. A big passion of mine has always been training horses and also rehabilitation. This channel is all about horse and rider wellbeing, and horse and rider training and development. You will find tips to improve your riding in and out of the saddle, and especially on how to develop a better seat in the saddle, which I think all good riding eventually comes down to.

I have worked with horses and riders for more than 20 years, first training horses and teaching riding in Finland where I live and also abroad. Later I studied to become a physiotherapist and after that also specialized in animal physiotherapy. I treat and train horses and riders, my biggest focus being to develop the connection and understanding between rider and the horse.

Welcome! I’m Dr. Linda Bluestein, an EDS patient & physician specializing in Ehlers-Danlos Syndromes & related disorders. I founded Hypermobility MD & Bendy Bodies to challenge outdated narratives & give people real answers, not dismissal.

Connective tissue disorders often mean chronic pain, repeated injuries, fatigue, autonomic symptoms, & bodies that don’t behave the way medicine expects them to. This channel exists to make sense of that complexity.

Each week, I share myth-busters, expert interviews, & practical strategies for managing pain, joint instability, fatigue, POTS, MCAS, & more. These conversations bridge science & lived experience—& remind us that being hard to diagnose is not the same as being difficult.

Subscribe & turn on notifications so you don’t miss anything.

Instagram: @hypermobilitymd

Explore Non-Surgical Treatments in a playlist of videos covering every type available, from medications to physical therapy to Chinese Medicine. In the Surgical Treatments playlist, watch a surgical walk-through video – a must see for anyone planning surgery for a cervical herniated disc.

The SURE FOOT Equine Stability Program® helps horses improve balance, relaxation, proprioception, and performance using SURE FOOT Pads.

On this channel, you’ll learn how to support your horse’s posture, movement, confidence, and long-term soundness—whether for training, rehabilitation, or everyday handling.

SURE FOOT Pads give horses the opportunity to explore their own balance. As they become more aware of how they are organized over their feet, many horses show reduced tension, improved movement, and greater comfort.

Wendy Murdoch, creator of SURE FOOT, shares how to:

Introduce pads safely
Choose the right pad types
Read your horse’s responses
Improve balance and body awareness
Support rehab, performance, and behavior

Used by horse owners, trainers, veterinarians, bodyworkers, and farriers, SURE FOOT helps horses become more relaxed, balanced, and confident.

row: The Animal Rescue League of Boston

Pets are family. This belief is at the heart of everything we do at the Animal Rescue League of Boston.

We are the first female-founded animal welfare organization in Massachusetts and are proud to carry on a legacy of kindness and compassion, helping more than 20,000 animals annually since 1899.

Recognized for our innovative, award-winning programs that go beyond sheltering, we address the root causes of the issues facing animals and the people who love them.

By partnering with communities, we help animals heal and thrive, keep pets and people together, and protect animals from harm.

Because there is no government funding for this important work, animals must rely on people like you to get the care they need, when they need it most, 365 days a year.

Welcome to my YouTube channel, a treasure trove of snippets of knowledge and handy hints in the field of veterinary neurology. 

Who am I? 
I bring expertise from specialist referral practice and academia to offer valuable insights and guidance. The aim is to breakdown down complex veterinary neurology concepts into digestible and practical tips.

What do I do? 
My research is dedicated to understanding cerebrospinal fluid disorders, particularly focusing on Canine Chiari malformation and syringomyelia. I am particularly passionate about raising awareness of diseases caused by selective breeding for poor head and body shape. I promote responsible breeding practices to minimize the suffering of animals affected by hereditary conditions.

Who is this channel for?
My content is accessible to both professionals and lay audiences. Join the community as you delve into the world of veterinary neurology. 

The views expressed are my own

We rescue cats from the streets in Romania, Carei and surrounding towns. We spay/neuter them and try to find them a forever home with responsible and loving owners.

We mostly need help with cat food as right now we have 188 cats, some very sick, some with dietary restrictions. We also cook for them but the food that we buy we try to get the best quality as medicine and treatments for the sick cost much more then good food that would prevent them from getting ill. Any help with cat food or small donations would be very welcome.

Innovative Treatment for Traumatic Brain Injuries

Plasticity® Brain Centers offers non-invasive neuro rehabilitation based on a single scientific principle: the brain is capable of learning and changing throughout a patient’s entire life. Our board-certified doctors and neurology specialists, supported by a hand-selected staff of patient care coordinators and therapists, provide you an innovative and comprehensive diagnostic and treatment model delivering exceptional outcomes to exceptional patients, unleashing your brain’s potential now.

Welcome to the YouTube channel of the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons (RCVS). 

Our role
We aim to enhance society through improved animal health and welfare. We do this by setting, upholding and advancing the educational, ethical and clinical standards of veterinary surgeons and veterinary nurses.

What we do 
As a statutory regulator, we are responsible under the Veterinary Surgeons Act 1966 for maintaining the UK Register of Veterinary Surgeons eligible to practise, setting standards for veterinary education and regulating the professional conduct of vets.

We also regulate vet nurses through our Royal Charter, including maintaining the Register of Veterinary Nurses and overseeing professional standards. The charter also enables us to award fellowships, diplomas and certificates.

Our videos
On this channel we share short films about our latest news and activities. We also run another channel dedicated to vet careers: http://www.youtube.com/vetcareers

We primarily take ex-breeding dogs but also take in a number of dogs from the pounds, public hand-ins and some from rescues abroad too. They often arrive needing veterinary care and our on site vet and volunteer vets spay and neuter all the adult dogs as well as carrying out other procedures such as treating ear/eye infections along with much bigger problems like orthopaedic surgeries, heart operations and cataract surgery. Please help us to keep going, things are particularly difficult at the moment and we are very worried but together we can save them all

Animal Rescue and Care (ARC) is a Kolkata based NGO registered under trust act in 2016 that has been working for the welfare of stray animals and their rights. The main objective of this organization is to create a better world for the voiceless friends by spreading awareness among people so that people live in harmony with the less privileged ones and defend their rights. 

ARC has two different shelters, the old one located in Kolkata District and a bigger rehabilitation shelter in Burdwan District.

ARC’ rescues animals those are ill or injured or animals those are subject to torture and abuse. ARC provides them relief, treatment, adequate care and a safe Refuge. ARC also provides shelter to senior and differently abled street dogs.
ARC conducts regular and organized ABC programs, proper Vaccination, De-worming and feeding drives with an aim that one day there will be no animal going to sleep with a hungry tummy or without a roof above his/her head.

When I met Bryan in 2014, he worked in insurance and had never had a pet! I owned my photography business of 20 years and lived in East Nashville. Moving to the country and starting a nonprofit rescue farm and animal sanctuary soon became a dream for both of us. Join us on this rescue journey, and together we can make a difference!

Fabled Farm Rescue & Sanctuary is a Middle TN based 501(c)3 committed to accepting and placing unwanted equines, farm animals, and kittens in qualified, loving forever homes, while continuing care for the unadoptable animals with medical or behavioral issues through our sanctuary program. In only a few short years Fabled Farm has helped over 500 animals and continues to expand its community outreach and programs.

We never meant to start Pet Angel Adoption. We didn't wake up one day and say "Let's start a cat rescue!" It started with two litter of kittens in Nancy and Jim Engel's backyard in little Frankenmuth, Michigan. When that two litter of kittens became cages of cats in the Engel Family's garage, Nancy and Jim realized what they had gotten into. They couldn't just stop saving kitties lives and finding them forever homes, so they rented out a building on List Street in Frankenmuth, moved the cats to the new location, and Pet Angel was born. 

Today, Pet Angel Adoption and Rescue is a volunteer-based, non-profit, no-kill cat shelter in that same building on List Street. We specialize in more than just the saving and rehoming of homeless, helpless and injured kitties, but we also offer awesome programs to the public in the Frankenmuth.

Purpose  – to provide quality information on common back and neck issues of horses and dogs. 
Intro - In an era where misinformation and traditional misunderstanding is rife amongst our printed and online sources this channel is aimed at providing a more balanced, much more scientific view on back and neck pain in dogs and horses. The information is built on 40 odd years of ongoing study and practical experience as a veterinarian working with horses and dogs, with the last 25 years being dedicated to problems related to upper body (especially back and neck) pain and dysfunction.
Topics to be pursued - In horses: Sacroiliac joint pain, Girthy horses, Saddle Fitting problems, Horses not forward, Irregularity of gait, poll shyness, Head tossing, Shoulder and hip strain.  In Dogs:  Paralyzed dogs, Disc disease, Yelping in pain, Stiff back, Loss of ability to Jump, Cruciate ligament strain, Hip dysplasia. Elbow dysplasia.   Equine and Canine Acupuncture, Equine and Canine Chiropractic.

The Gazette in Janesville, Wisconsin, is an award-winning newspaper covering Rock and Walworth counties. The Gazette was named Wisconsin’s Newspaper of the Year four years in a row and GazetteXtra.com the state’s best newspaper website six out of the last eight years.

The Gazette and GazetteXtra.com feature news, sports, opinion, features and blogs under one unifying idea: Local matters.

The Gazette is the oldest business in Janesville.

Levi Alden and Z.A. Stoddard launched The Janesville Gazette in 1845 as a weekly newspaper with 300 subscribers. Howard F. Bliss acquired the company in 1883 and passed it to his son Harry H. Bliss in 1919. Harry's sons Sidney H. and Robert W. succeeded their father in 1937. Skip Bliss acquired the company as publisher and president in 1992. Adams Publishing Group acquired the newspaper in 2019.

GazetteXtra.com launched in 1997.

A simple six step approach is used to solve conditions affecting horses and equid species for centuries: 
1. History of the condition
2. KISS Theory (Keep It Simple Stupid)
3. Anatomy and "Ologies"
4. Form=Function
5. The Curiosity of Why?
6.Thinking for Yourself!

Come join her for the ride of undiagnosed horses in the field of equine sports medicine!

row: Restore Therapy Scar Training and Scar Clinic

Emma Holly at Restore Therapy is the leading educator in Britain on the subject of scars for manual therapists and over 2,000 therapists have enrolled onto the Restore Therapy courses. She teaches scar therapy courses online and in-person and lectures internationally. Therapist training courses are available around the UK, Australia and New Zealand and online.  Private clinic appointments with Emma in London’s most prestigious medical address, Harley Street.

Scar therapy is used to improve feeling and functionality in the scar and surrounding tissues, creating better movement between the layers of the skin, fascia (connective tissue) and muscle. Using non-invasive methods to help mature or new scars and complications associated with surgery and trauma such as fibrosis and adhesions.  See www.restoretherapy.co.uk for training details and www.restoretherapyclinic.co.uk to book a private scar therapy treatment with Emma in Harley Street.

row: Angels Among Us Pet Rescue, Inc. is a 501(c)(3), non-profit, volunteer-based organization dedicated to rescuing dogs and cats from high-kill shelters in North Georgia. It was created in February 2009 by a group of people in the Atlanta area who wanted to do more to save the many adoptable dogs and cats who found themselves on death row in Georgia animal control facilities. Our motto is “Rescue One Until There are None.” As of May 12, 2021 we have rescued more than 18,000 dogs and cats. Most of these animals came into our program from high-kill animal control facilities throughout Georgia.  If you want to make a difference and help animal rescue in Georgia, you can donate, adopt a pet, foster a pet, or volunteer your time to advocate for animal welfare policies in Georgia, like low cost spay neuter, anti-tethering and protections for K9 officers and dogs in hot cars.

Hundreds of thousands of healthy and treatable cats and dogs are being abandoned and killed in pounds, shelters and vet clinics each year in Australia.
 
This is preventable.
 
Getting to Zero (G2Z) aims to increase responsibility for companion animals so that every community and municipality can achieve zero euthanasia of all healthy and treatable cats and dogs.
 
G2Z is relevant to state governments, local government, pounds, shelters, rescue groups, breed organisations, breeders, pet shops, animal trainers, groomers, wildlife organisations, veterinarians, and all community members who are concerned about better management and welfare of cats and dogs.
The Getting to Zero Model details the principles, structures and strategies for achieving zero killing of healthy and treatable cats and dogs (more than 90% of all incoming stray and surrendered cats and dogs) in whole communities.

Go to www.g2z.org.au to find out more.

row: Active Animal Physiotherapy Dr Lesley Goff

Dr. Lesley Goff is one of the world’s leading Animal Physiotherapists, currently balancing her animal physiotherapy practice with presenting at vet/physio conferences and lecturing/teaching to physiotherapists and equine science students. Lesley’s career as a physiotherapist spans over 20 years in which time, following her initial physiotherapy degree, she has completed master’s level degrees in Manipulative Physiotherapy, Exercise and Sports Science and Animal Physiotherapy. More recently Lesley completed her doctorate at the University of Queensland, paving the way for further research into the equine sacroiliac joint.Dr. Lesley Goff is often consulted by, and provides training for other practitioners in the area of sacroiliac joint injury. She has been involved in teaching on the Animal Physiotherapy masters degree at University of Queensland and has lectured to both veterinarians and physiotherapists, and presented courses in Australia, Scandinavia, USA, South Africa and the UK.

Soul Dog is a 501 (c)(3) nonprofit animal rescue organization founded with the mission to spay/neuter and protect animals. Soul Dog is proactive in animal welfare, advancing the need for spaying and neutering our pets to reduce overpopulation. We travel to rural communities on Native American reservations, where spaying and neutering will only happen if it is nearly free or very convenient. Soul Dog works with volunteer veterinarians to provide the spaying and neutering service at no cost to the public. Donations are used to defray the costs associated with medications, supplies, and the operating cost for clinics.

Our Mission:
Soul Dog Rescue performs collaborative, targeted work, primarily through spay/neuter, in underserved regions in order to create sustainable change and promote cultural shifts regarding the treatment of companion animals.

Maria Ines Gay da Fonseca Allgayer is a Brazilian DVM and Equine Therapist with larger experience as an equine practitioner for more the 20 years. In 2005, Dr. Allgayer opened her own practice “Equivet” and in 2007 she opened her first Equine Rehabilitation Center. 
In 2011, she moved to the U.S. and opened her first Equine Rehabilitation Center, Therapy4Horses, Oklahoma. 
In 2016, Dr. Allgayer was invited to be member of the Veterinary Equine Therapist Team for the Olympic International Committee of the 2016 Olympic Games in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
 In 2018, she was a member of the Uruguayan and Argentinian Veterinary Team for the World Equestrian Games held in Mill Spring, North Carolina, U.S. 
Since 2014, she has been offering courses in Equine Rehabilitation in her own facilities.

Dr Neil J. Davies D.C, is a reputed chiropractic author and educator. As the author of Clinical Paediatrics A Clinical Handbook, Churchill Livingstone (2000 & 2010), he became well known for post-graduate chiropractic education in teaching the prudent examination and care of children. From 2000, he traveled widely and presented seminars in many countries helping chiropractors better understand excellence in clinical care for children of all ages.

Dr Davies developed a system or technique of subluxation assessment and treatment initially taught as Adjusting the Child and later evolving to the NeuroImpulse Protocol, also known as NIP. This is still taught widely in many countries and has a popular folowing.

Dr Davies developed a range of clinical educational teaching products and his latest online learning resource is called NIP Academy which is free for chiropractors to join at the Bronze level and allows upgrades inside for more materials. It includes seminars in streaming video.

DCH Animal Adoptions, which stands for "dogs, cats and horses", is a NSW-based non-profit animal rescue charity (CFN 18284) committed to the rescue and rehoming of unwanted and neglected domestic animals - mainly dogs, cats and horses - but occasionally other animals such as rabbits and guinea pigs.
Our volunteers rescue animals from certain death in Sydney's pounds and shelters, and horses from the knackery and ensure they are provided with veterinary attention and foster care until a permanent and loving home can be found.
The foster care system benefits you and the foster pet. By providing you with valuable information about the animal gained through the carer's experiences in a home environment, we can help match you up with the right pet for your home. The animals also benefit from being in a loving home environment until their permanent homes are found.

Named after a rescued horse saved nearly 30 years ago, Friends of Lackota Animal Sanctuary was founded to give animals a second chance at life. The sanctuary began when a young boy refused to let Lackota go to slaughter—working hard to save him and, in the process, finding a lifelong purpose.

Located in Northern Colorado, we specialize in rescuing horses and donkeys from the slaughter pipeline, but no animal is turned away if we can provide proper care. Many arrive from kill pens or auctions, often neglected, afraid, and broken. Here, they receive love, rehabilitation, and safety—whether they find a forever home or remain at the sanctuary.

Our mission is simple: help animals beat the odds and live the life they deserve.

Friends of Rescue Animals (FRAs) is an all-volunteer 501(c)(3) non-profit organization founded in 2004. Our organization has grown to over 300 volunteers, and with this growth, we now support two municipal shelters -- Rowlett, TX and Garland, TX – and operate our own cat rescue program.  FRAs has helped countless pets avoid euthanasia, find their forever homes and live longer, healthier lives.

Our mission is to provide resources, programs and education to promote adoption and care of homeless pets in our community. FRAs’ vision is a world where every companion animal has a safe and loving forever home. 

Our organizational programs include operating the volunteer program for both shelters, providing funding for heartworm treatments and emergency medical care, accepting cats from the shelter and citizens into our foster-based cat rescue, supporting TNR/SNR efforts for community cats and most recently funding dog transport initiatives.

We rescue unwanted, abused, neglected, or abandoned equines; provide them with care and rehabilitation; and finally find them a compatible, loving home.  We believe that education is the long-term solution to improving the lives of equines.

Our goal is to aid abused, neglected, starving, and unwanted horses from surrenders, animal control, or auctions. We provide food, training, and veterinary care for their recovery. Post-recovery, they're evaluated and put up for adoption to approved homes. Economic challenges have led to increased horse sales but fewer buyers, resulting in more horses in danger. Many are abandoned or auctioned. We offer these horses a temporary haven until a permanent, loving home is found.

We are committed to saving the animals that are often overlooked and under-appreciated at local shelters; this includes, the sick, injured, senior and neonatal kittens and their mothers. We are dedicated to helping those special needs animals find their forever homes.

Our rescue and adoption process is sustainable, innovative and effective. In 2015, we rescued and adopted out over one thousand dogs and cats from shelters throughout the state of Utah.

row: Paralyzed Pup Go- How I cared for my dog Jasper

Paralyzed Pup Go- Remembering Jasper.

This channel shares Jasper’s journey. After becoming paralyzed when he was eight, for nine years he used his wheelchair and our specially designed Changing Station and Tub-Sling to live his best life. Jasper inspired us every day with his determination and joyful spirit.

The Changing Station is a supportive, multi-use devise used daily to change diapers, express the bladder and keep Jasper upright and comfortable—not to mention less stressful on my back!

It serves as a standing support for physical therapy, healthcare and grooming, It can be converted into a Tub-Sling support for bathing.

We hope Jasper’s story inspires others caring for paralyzed pets.

*PATENT PENDING

Disclaimer:
Always consult with a qualified professional to determine what is best for your pet. Professional guidance is recommended to ensure their safety and well-being.

The International Chiropractors Association (ICA) has stood the test of time. We are the world’s oldest international chiropractic professional organization. We represent chiropractors, students, chiropractic assistants, educators, and laypersons world-wide.

The ICA is dedicated to the growth and development of the chiropractic profession based on Dr. Palmer’s fundamental belief in the principle and philosophy of chiropractic as a unique, separate, distinct, and drug-less health care profession. We believe in ‘staying in the lane of chiropractic’.

ICA’s distinguishing feature today is the same as it was in 1926 – advocating for chiropractic. For over 94 years, the ICA has advocated and, when necessary, litigated to support the chiropractic profession and quality patient care. With the support of ICA’s dedicated members and leaders globally, chiropractic is a formally recognized and respected health care choice.

My name is Reanna Whitnall, owner of Renew Massage & Healing Arts. I am a Certified Massage Therapist with over 20 years of experience. I am also a Certified Group Fitness Instructor and Orthopedic Exercise Specialist.
I specialize in treating clients with chronic pain and injuries. Part of my job is educating my clients on how to take better care of their bodies. With massage I can provide significant relief from severe pain, but without proper self care the effects are temporary, and symptoms can return. 
My number one recommendation is to stretch daily. It is so overlooked by most people, but it is essential for releasing tight muscles, reducing pain, and preventing injury. I hope to provide you with easy to follow guides to stretching, massage, myofascial release and other self care practices to help you maintain optimal wellness. 
Please use caution when attempting any stretches or massage techniques. Consult your physician if you are recovering from an injury or post surgery.

I eventually learned to incorporate Tui Na and other techniques into my own massage routines, but today my most popular routines are chair massages which include PNF Tech Therapy. These routines are especially helpful to office workers who suffer from tight rhomboids, head-forward postures, and other symptoms of "office worker syndrome." PNF Tech Therapy is based on the Kaya Kalp healing system as it was practiced in Tibet many centuries ago, and I practice those techniques with an open heart and love for all life.

I am a therapist with over 30 years of clinical experience gained in Poland, the United Kingdom, Norway, and France. I combine the perspectives of physiotherapy and massage therapy, and over the years I have developed my own therapeutic approach — along with many unique techniques and practical tools — as a result of decades of experience, dozens of completed trainings, and my own developed methods, all integrated into one coherent and practical system.
I do not believe in one-size-fits-all protocols. Instead, I teach clinical reasoning and individualized treatment planning, so you can select safe, effective, and appropriate techniques for each client. My goal is not only to demonstrate techniques, but also to help you understand the underlying causes of dysfunction, recognize overload patterns and compensations, and restore functional balance in the body. If you are looking to deepen your skills and improve your clinical outcomes, you are welcome to join my training.

Regenerative Stem Cell Therapy & Pet Rehabilitation at Safari Veterinary Care Centers in League City, TX.

Stem Cells live in all tissues of the body and lay dormant until there is damage in need of repair.

The body’s natural repair process sends healing cells to the area of injury and directs these healing cells as to what needs to be done. In all cases these healing cells are stem cells. However, in many cases, the regenerative process is overwhelmed or exhausted or out of resources and healing is incomplete and that’s where regenerative medicine comes in.

Regenerative medicine strives to use the body’s own healing mechanisms, by adding Platelet Rich Plasma and/or stem cells we can restart the healing process which rejuvenates the damaged tissues and rebuilds damaged or missing tissues.

Stem Cells (don't heal, they) regenerate the original cartilage tissue just as it was when the animal was an infant.

Hours: M-F: 6am-8am; Sat & Sun: 9am-6pm

As an Esalen Massage Therapist in Atlanta GA, I offer videos educational videos about Esalen Massage therapy. I specialize in Esalen massage: a full-body contemplative massage.  The hallmarks of Esalen massage are long flowing strokes, rocking, stretches, and holds. The goal of Esalen massage is to help the client enter into a deeply relaxed, meditative state.

The Esalen practitioner responds to the unique issues presented by the individual client, instead of imposing a particular protocol, form or set way of working. Each massage is customized to meet your personal needs in the moment.

Created at the Esalen Institute in Big Sur, CA, Esalen Massage was designed to give the client a sense of deep relaxation and integration of body, mind, and spirit.

OUR APPROACH
Our goal is to get you out of pain and keep you that way. That is our bottom line.
When our doctors do an initial evaluation, we will have a good idea if your condition is something we can fix or not. If we can fix it, we will explain to you what the problem is, how it will be fixed and about how long it will take. Once we get you out of pain, we will work with you to help keep you that way and prevent reinjury. Our job is to fix the injury and release you. We do not want to see you back in our office repeatedly or for a long term plan.

AlphaFlo® is a canine amniotic tissue allograft that was created to supplement and protect canine tissues.  AlphaFlo® is comprised of cytokines, growth factors, and extracellular matrix proteins that are naturally found in amniotic tissues. The use of canine amniotic tissue allografts to supplement and protect tissues in canines may be minimally invasive, safe, and offer a morbidity profile comparable to or better than those of existing modalities.

Amniotic tissues possess reported anti-inflammatory, anti-microbial, anti-fibrotic, and regenerative properties that make it attractive for use in veterinary applications.

Tissues are recovered from healthy dogs during live birth by Licensed Veterinarians using safe recovery techniques and sterile equipment without harm to the animals. Allografts are subject to stringent USP testing prior to release for implantation. Ask your Vet about AlphaFlo®

The McTimoney Animal Association is the professional body for McTimoney Animal Practitioners. The McTimoney Animal Association exists to promote excellence in animal chiropractic for its members, and to the veterinary and animal-owning communities.

McTimoney is a form of chiropractic manipulation used to treat pain and dysfunction of the musculoskeletal system. It predominantly focuses on optimising alignment of the spine and pelvis in order to restore correct function of the skeletal system, nervous system and surrounding soft tissue. The technique is non-invasive and gentle and is readily accepted by animals. The treatment aims to resolve dysfunction and balance the animal’s musculoskeletal system, restoring health and movement, soundness and performance.

row: AKB Dressage and Soft Tissue Therapy

Female Equestrian with a passion for Dressage. Full time groom in Dorset and part time Sports Massage therapist for Humans (OSSM level 5)and Horses (Equissage Europe). Had my own horse since 11years old but sadly sold my dressage horse around 7years ago and have since trained and competed on my employers horses. Up until 2020 the horses we had on the yard were not for dressage but since then we have purchased the lovely Hanoverian Finnick SR and our training and competing has commenced and so far been pretty successful. I suppose the dream is to go the nationals, however every outing we have i see as learning and training. The scores and frills are all a bonus. I enjoy doing groundwork with all the horses and vary their work with regular hacking, polework, jumping, lunging, inhand poles and schooling. please enjoy following our adventures.

Adopt: View our available cats at purrpartners.org.

Foster: Become the bridge between rescue and adoption.

Support: Your donations fund life-saving medical care.

Hi, I'm Katie Mehrtens, and I am the owner of The Right Spot Pet Massage.  I am a nationally certified small animal massage therapist and offer therapeutic massage for all breeds of dogs, cats, and other small animals. 

I created this channel to share some of my knowledge about pet massage with you. My intention is to provide you with some at-home tools you can use with your pet.  

Please know that all animals are different and will react / respond differently to massage. So, what works one time or on one pet may not work the next time or on another pet. Never force the massage – if your pet does not want to be massaged, stop and try again another time.

A few notes:
• These are simply informative videos
• Massage is not a replacement for veterinary care
• See your vet if your pet seems to be in pain
• Never massage deep on your pet. The idea of “it will hurt now, but feel better later” does not apply to animals
 
Thanks so much for tuning in!
Please enjoy these videos!

International Animal Rescue Goa was established as a charity (Registration No : 106/GOA/98) in August 1998. Our aim is to reduce the terrible suffering of animals in Goa.

Since we began this vital work, International Animal Rescue Goa, has sterilized more than 30,000 dogs, 11,000 cats, and vaccinated over 60,000 dogs against rabies. Our ambulances have collected thousands of road casualties and we have made a major impact on mange, which causes intense suffering and was endemic within the street dog community. We rescue dozens of animals from wells every year, have rescued hundreds of snakes from houses and snake charmers which would otherwise have been killed or died, and do our best to educate the public on animal welfare issues.

Heavenly Paws Animal Rescue, Inc. is a 501 (c) non-profit, all-volunteer, no-kill feline rescue.

Angeline Behrendt, a trained Veterinary Technician, founded Heavenly Paws Animal Shelter, Inc. in 2004 to expand her services and provide safe and secure homes for cats.

Heavenly Paws Animal Shelter is not a true brick-and-mortar shelter. We have a network of foster homes to take in and care for homeless cats until permanent, loving homes can be found. We also strive to help humans understand the importance of controlling the pet population through spaying and neutering.

Heavenly Paws Animal Shelter relies on private and corporate donations to help fund our rescue operations and accomplish our mission.

Heavenly Paws Animal Shelter has treated and saved many cats in challenging situations. All of our volunteers have pledged to rescue as many cats as possible with the space and funding we have available. We will always be committed to saving lives, one stray at a time!

row:
Here at Widom Chiropractic, we are proud to help our patients live better lives without pain.

We truly believe that nobody deserves to live in pain, even as they age, and we will do everything we can to ensure that our patients are comfortable. We are proud to help people after accidents or injuries and when they are uncomfortable doing their day-to-day activities.

Though pain itself is uncomfortable, when you have chronic pain, life can become unbearable. You may struggle just doing your normal day-to-day tasks. You may have trouble concentrating because you are not feeling well.

After a thorough examination with X-rays, we will be able to determine where your problem lies and discuss how we can help you feel better. Even after just a few treatments, you will be amazed at how much better you feel! You will be able to move around better, have better circulation, and may even start to lose weight. Chiropractic care can really make a world of difference to you!

Each Acupressure Massage session I do is tailored specifically to the individual animal to address any issues the animal may be experiencing. It could be anxiety, arthritis, general aging, etc. I currently have an office in Sedona, Arizona and work in veterinary offices, and canine rehab clinic. Last year I added vibrational sound therapy using crystal singing bowls to my available services. I am amazed at how effective vibration can be with animals. Even deaf animals benefit. I spend quite a bit of time at a senior dog sanctuary in Prescott, Arizona and they have taught me so much about the benefits of sound therapy. I will be adding many videos at the sanctuary so you can see for yourself.

With Love,
Tracey

Species we rescue include possums and gliders, koalas, kangaroos and wallabies, wombats, echidnas, turtles, snakes, lizards, all native birds (including owls and raptors).

Established in 1978, Hunter Wildlife Rescue (formerly Native Animal Trust Fund) was the first volunteer run wildlife rescue organisation in NSW.

row:
Pamper Your Pup with a Massage

Dog massage therapist = my dream job! Being a dog massage therapist is my dream job! It is not only a profession to me, but it is also my calling. I have committed myself to a lifetime of improving the quality of life of dogs. I have mastered every manual technique for their unique anatomy so I can improve their wellbeing.
I could not imagine myself doing anything else because nothing is closer to my heart than my furry friends and working with them gives me the greatest pleasure. The moment I saw the happiness of my first canine client I knew this was my path. I believe it is important not to take dogs out of their everyday environment, so I do in-home massages. I can perform dog massage therapy anywhere requested, but the smell of home and familiar surroundings is key in helping your dog achieve relaxation. This way, there are no distractions, and we can focus on complete unwinding and healing during the session.

Not Another Vet Nurse (NAVN) seeks to bring awareness, change, and possibly end the stigma of mental health and suicide within veterinary medicine. Not only is the veterinary profession among the top for suicide concerns but the statistics regarding mental health are just as alarming. 1 in 10 Veterinarians has suffered severe psychological distress. 1 in 6 have considered suicide. 1 in 5 have been a victim or knows someone who has been a victim of cyber bullying. 

NAVN is a 501(c)(3) public charity for veterinary professionals to be able to afford mental health care. All funds donated through our organization goes directly back into the veterinary community.

By restoring the correct movement of the joints, particularly those of the spine, the animal becomes better able to maintain its own health and achieve its full potential within its field.

Equine-Alignment care should be used alongside traditional veterinary care to enhance the wellbeing of the horse. 

Steve Treloar's Equine Align care may help to:
Provide gentle musculoskeletal alignment for the enhancement of movement or performance, of your horse and Integrate its movement to enhance performance

Steve Treloar's qualifications include:
​
Bachelor of Applied Science (Chiropractor)
Cert BT—Certified Equine Bowen Therapist (ISBT)
Certified Equine Rehabilitation and Training (ACAAT)

Equine Chiropractic will address a number of potential health and performance issues. It is not designed to be a replacement for traditional medical horse care, but is instead intended to keep your horse in peak condition.

Even in the most athletic horse there can be abnormalities in the animal's gait or simply movement habits that mean the horse does not perform up to its full potential. Chiropractic has been found to be extremely effective in dealing with such issues, as well as alleviating neck and back discomfort.

Chiropractic detects spinal, limbs, and pelvic dysfunctions. By using hand thrust manoeuvres it releases tension and realigns the horses skeleton.  Spinal alignments stop neuro connection at the vertebral level and the correction recreates normal flow between the central and peripheral nervous systems. 

If your horse undergoes a chiropractic treatment, it will benefit from improved interactions between the spine's biomechanics and neurological signals.

row: Hi I'm Sara. I am a professional Equine Sports Massage Therapist working in Wiltshire, Hampshire, Somerset and Dorset. As part of my work I take videos of horses walking and trotting and slow them down using the SloMo app on my iPad. This helps me understand where the horse isn't moving correctly and where it may have aches and pains. I can then perform a full body massage on the horse and explain to the owner how the horse can be rehabilitated and restore full movement to the affected area(s). I always massage the whole of the horse as all the muscles are interlinked and compensate for the movement of each other and it is pointless working on one muscle just for another to become sore.

Welcome to Virginia Farm Animal Sanctuary (VFAS)  — a place of lifelong sanctuary for farm animals in need of a forever home.

Many of the animals here were once beloved pets whose families experienced life changes such as illness, loss, relocation, downsizing, or other circumstances beyond their control. When care needed a new place to continue, VFAS became that place.

Our mission is simple: provide lifelong sanctuary, compassionate care, and peace of mind for both animals and the people who love them.

Follow along for daily life at the sanctuary, animal stories, behind-the-scenes moments, educational content, tours, special events, and the frequent funny farm moment.

Home to donkeys, goats, sheep, pigs, llamas, poultry, and more, every resident here has a story — and every story matters.

Rehabilitation Center: 
Pets benefit from rehabilitation much as humans benefit from physical therapy.  Rehabilitation helps pets recover from injury or surgery, regain and maintain mobility and decrease pain. 

Behavior & Training Classes:
Recognizing the relationship between physical and mental health, we augment our medical, surgical and dental services with behavior and training opportunities for both cats and dogs.

row: Subjects in Spinal Cord Injury Rehabilitation

This channel serves to provide education material for patients, their families and friends and non-medical laypeople on Spinal cord injuries (SCI), how they can affect functioning in everyday lives and how the use of therapy techniques with your therapist or at home can be implemented to improve participation in everyday activities.  Subjects will range from ADLs (activities such as activities as feeding, grooming and dressing) transfers from different surfaces and upper extremity management after a SCI; which all can become more difficult after a SCI.
These videos are for educational purposes only, and one should consult their medical doctor and/or rehabilitation specialist (physical or occupational therapist prior to implementing anything seen in theses videos.
